title: Tsinghua news: RANA refresh-optimized eDRAM for neural acceleration (ISCA 2018)
supports: RANA (Tu et al., ISCA 2018): retention-aware training + hybrid computation pattern + refresh-optimized eDRAM controller; authors claim 99.7% of eDRAM refreshes removed with negligible accuracy loss (via search snippet) [B4-03, B4-06]

title: Tsinghua news (Chinese): RANA
supports: Chinese release: vs SRAM accelerators at equal area, RANA cuts off-chip accesses 41.7% and system energy 66.2% (authors' claim) (via search snippet) [B4-03]

title: Refresh Triggered Computation: Improving the Energy Efficiency of CNN Accelerators
supports: Describes RANA as disabling refresh when data lifetime in an eDRAM bank is shorter than the cell retention time (via search snippet) [B4-03]

title: EDEN: Enabling Energy-Efficient, High-Performance DNN Inference Using Approximate DRAM (MICRO 2019)
supports: DNN inference on DRAM run below nominal voltage/latency; 21% average DRAM energy saving (29% YOLO/VGG) within 1% accuracy; up to 17% speedup; DNNs tolerate the resulting bit errors (via search snippet) [B4-01, B4-04]

title: EnforceSNN: reduced-voltage approximate DRAM for spiking neural networks
supports: Reduced-voltage approximate DRAM for SNNs, up to 84.9% DRAM energy saving (via search snippet) [B4-04]

title: RAIDR: Retention-Aware Intelligent DRAM Refresh (ISCA 2012)
supports: Two retention bins give 74.6% refresh reduction with no DRAM change and 1.25 KB storage (32 GB, 8-core); 16.1% average DRAM power reduction, 8.6% performance gain; Bloom filters hold bins (via search snippet) [B4-02, B4-08]

title: Retrospective: RAIDR: Retention-Aware Intelligent DRAM Refresh
supports: Retrospective: ~75%+ of refreshes removable; benefits grow with DRAM chip capacity (via search snippet) [B4-02]

title: Multi-level DRAM sensing scheme (US 5,917,748)
supports: Cites T. Murotani et al., 'A 4-level storage 4 Gb DRAM', ISSCC 1997 TP4.6 p.74: four-level sensing of 2 bits per DRAM cell; cell capacitor must be ~3x larger than for single-bit storage (via search snippet; NEC affiliation not confirmed) [B4-05]

title: US5909619A: Method for forming a DRAM cell and array to store two-bit data
supports: DRAM cell storing two bits as four charge levels using combined stacked + trench capacitor (via search snippet) [B4-05]

title: 70% Size, 100% Accuracy: Lossless LLM Compression via Dynamic-Length Float (DFloat11)
supports: BF16 exponent carries ~2.6 bits of entropy in 8 bits (~40 of 256 values used); sign/mantissa near full entropy; Huffman-coded exponents give ~11 bits/weight, ~30% size reduction, bit-identical outputs; GPU decompression kernel; 405B on 8x80GB (via search snippet) [B4-04, B4-07, B4-08]

title: DFloat11 poster, NeurIPS 2025
supports: DFloat11 accepted at NeurIPS 2025 (via search snippet) [B4-07]

title: Structera XA: CXL compression, every gigabyte counts
supports: Marvell hardware LZ4 compression in CXL memory expanders; marketing claims physical DRAM turned into 2x/4x/8x useful capacity (vendor claim) (via search snippet) [B4-07, B4-20]

title: Marvell Structera X 3406/3506 six-channel CXL 3.2 memory expander
supports: Structera X 3406/3506 deliver 2-3x effective capacity depending on workload via onboard LZ4; X 2504 has four inline LZ4 engines (via search snippet) [B4-07, B4-20]

title: Compression algorithm and block size for OCP CXL memory expanders (IEEE CAL 2026)
supports: A slower, more complex compression algorithm and different block size can raise expander capacity and cut access latency because DRAM traffic drops (via search snippet) [B4-07, B4-17]

title: Seagate working on composable memory appliance with CXL memory
supports: ZeroPoint DenseMem claims 2-3x effective CXL Type 3 capacity; demonstrated with Seagate at OCP Global Summit 2025 (via search snippet) [B4-07, B4-20]

title: Block-level compression for CXL memory expanders (arXiv 2603.26131)
supports: Block-level compression for memory expanders for larger effective capacity (IBEX, accepted ISC 2026 per snippet; attribution of this arXiv ID to IBEX not pinned) (via search snippet) [B4-07]

title: KIVI: A Tuning-Free Asymmetric 2bit Quantization for KV Cache (ICML 2024)
supports: Keys quantised per-channel, values per-token, recent residual tokens kept full precision; 2-bit KV cuts peak memory 2.6x (incl. weights) with little accuracy loss; up to 4x batch, 2.35-3.47x throughput (via search snippet) [B4-05, B4-06, B4-07, B4-09]

title: Ambit: In-Memory Accelerator for Bulk Bitwise Operations Using Commodity DRAM (MICRO-50)
supports: Triple-row activation gives bitwise majority (AND/OR with a constant row); dual-contact cells give NOT; ~1% DRAM area; 32x performance and 35x energy vs state of the art on seven bulk bitwise ops (via search snippet) [B4-09, B4-10, B4-19]

title: Ambit publication page
supports: Ambit with 8 banks: 44x bulk bitwise throughput vs Intel Skylake (via search snippet) [B4-10]

title: A Modern Primer on Processing in Memory
supports: ComputeDRAM showed that violating timing between activations mimics Ambit's triple-row activation in some off-the-shelf DRAM chips (via search snippet) [B4-10, B4-19]

title: SIMDRAM: An End-to-End Framework for Bit-Serial SIMD Computing in DRAM
supports: Bit-serial SIMD computing in DRAM built on RowClone and Ambit primitives (only background section seen; no SIMDRAM numbers used) (via search snippet) [B4-09, B4-19]

title: Celestial AI wants to break the memory wall, fuse HBM with DDR5
supports: Photonic Fabric memory transactions ~6.2 pJ/bit vs ~62.5 pJ/bit via NVLink/NVSwitch (company claim); 120 ns round trip; module of 2 HBM stacks (72 GB) + 4 DDR5 DIMMs (up to 2 TB) (via search snippet) [B4-13, B4-14, B4-21]

title: HOTI25: Celestial AI's Photonic Fabric
supports: Hot Interconnects 2025: ~2.4 pJ/bit fabric, ~300 ns server-to-memory latency; 16-module appliance with 32 TB DDR5, HBM as write-through cache (company claims) (via search snippet) [B4-13, B4-14, B4-21]

title: A 0.54 pJ/b 20 Gb/s ground-referenced single-ended short-reach serial link in 28 nm CMOS
supports: GRS link: 20 Gb/s at 0.54 pJ/bit over 4.5 mm of organic substrate, forwarded clock, 28 nm (via search snippet) [B4-15]

title: A 1.17 pJ/b, 25 Gb/s/pin ground-referenced single-ended serial link (JSSC 2019)
supports: 25 Gb/s/pin GRS at 1.17 pJ/bit with matched-delay clock forwarding, for MCM and short package-to-package channels; 2018 CICC lists the 2013 link at 0.58 pJ/b (via search snippet) [B4-15]

title: US12405629B2: High-speed signaling system with ground referenced signaling (GRS) over substrate
supports: GRS link between devices (e.g., CPU-GPU) with N data lanes and forwarded clock over substrate (via search snippet) [B4-15]

title: ArchShield: Architectural Framework for Assisting DRAM Scaling by Tolerating High Error Rates (ISCA 2013)
supports: ECC DIMMs alone tolerate ~1 faulty cell per million; ArchShield (fault map + selective word-level replication) tolerates error rates up to 1e-4 at 4% capacity and <2% performance on an 8 GB DIMM (via search snippet) [B4-01, B4-02, B4-08]

title: Architectural Techniques to Enable Reliable and Scalable Memory Systems (thesis)
supports: Thesis copy describing ArchShield's tolerance of 100x higher error rates than ECC alone (via search snippet) [B4-01]

title: Kelle: Co-design KV Caching and eDRAM for Efficient LLM Serving in Edge Computing
supports: eDRAM as primary KV store on edge devices; two-dimensional adaptive refresh policy; attention-based eviction and recomputation shortens data lifetime; reported 3.9x speedup, 4.5x energy saving (figures via a mirror abstract, not verified) (via search snippet) [B4-03, B4-06]

title: SHIELD: A Segmented Hierarchical Memory Architecture for Energy-Efficient LLM Inference on Edge NPUs
supports: Separates sign/exponent from mantissa; KV mantissa tolerates BER up to 1e-4 before long-context degradation; transient activations degrade above 1e-6; relaxed 1216 us refresh for KV mantissa; 35% refresh-energy reduction (via search snippet) [B4-04, B4-05, B4-06]

title: BitROM: Weight Reload-Free CiROM Architecture Towards Billion-Parameter 1.58-bit LLM Inference
supports: KV entries accessed every decoding step are implicitly refreshed if token-to-token time stays below the ~64 ms retention time (via search snippet) [B4-03, B4-19]

title: Sectored DRAM: A Practical Energy-Efficient and High-Performance Fine-Grained DRAM Architecture
supports: Fine-grained activation and transfer cut DRAM energy up to 33% (20% avg); 89% of Half-DRAM's performance benefit with 12% less energy and 34% less area; activation energy saving ~6% avg; row overfetch 1-2 KB per 64 B (via search snippet) [notes: rejected sub-page idea; B4-09 context]

title: Sandisk and SK hynix begin global standardization of High Bandwidth Flash (HBF)
supports: HBF targeted at bandwidth comparable to HBM with up to 8-16x HBM capacity at similar cost (company claim) (via search snippet) [B4-16, B4-21]

title: SK hynix sets first HBF standard for AI memory
supports: First OCP technical specification for High Bandwidth Flash released (Aug 2026) (via search snippet) [B4-16]

title: HBF open standard for AI inference: 512GB
supports: HBF 256 GB per die, 512 GB per 16-high stack, 1.6 TB/s read bandwidth (via search snippet) [B4-16, B4-21]

title: Flash getting stacked high-bandwidth version
supports: HBF has higher latency and larger pages than HBM; slow writes make it suited to inference with static weights, not training (via search snippet) [B4-16]

title: High Bandwidth Flash became a spec today, not a product you can buy
supports: HBF OCP spec released 2026-08-03; first samples were scheduled 2H26 and HBF inference devices early 2027; 2.2%-of-unlimited-HBM result is simulated (via search snippet) [B4-16]

title: RangeGuard: Efficient, Bounded Approximate Error Correction for Reliable DNNs
supports: BF16 weights/activations (ResNet-50, Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.2-1B): sign and mantissa flips negligible until BER 1e-5; exponent flips catastrophic even at BER 1e-12 (via search snippet) [B4-04, B4-05]

title: Bit-Flip Error Resilience in LLMs: A Comprehensive Analysis and Defense Framework (EMNLP 2025)
supports: Analysis of bit flips across LLM parameters/activations/gradients; FlipGuard protects exponent bits (via search snippet) [B4-04]

title: DRAM Scaling Trend and Beyond (J. Choe)
supports: Cell capacitance <10 fF at D1z/D1a, ~5-6 fF projected at 1c; >7 fF needs k>50 (CROSS-REF from dram-moonshot Phase A logs; not re-opened by B4) [B4-01]

title: IEEE TC paper on DRAM refresh (B. Jacob group)
supports: Refresh >20% of DRAM energy at 32Gb (simulation) (CROSS-REF from dram-moonshot Phase A logs; not re-opened by B4) [B4-02, B4-20]

title: Improving DRAM Performance by Parallelizing Refreshes with Accesses (HPCA 2014)
supports: 16.6% average performance loss from refresh at 32Gb even with per-bank refresh (CROSS-REF from dram-moonshot Phase A logs; not re-opened by B4) [B4-02, B4-03]

title: TrendForce press release on HBM vs DDR5 die size and yield
supports: HBM die 35-45% larger than DDR5 at same node/capacity; HBM yield incl. TSV packaging 20-30% lower (CROSS-REF from dram-moonshot Phase A logs; not re-opened by B4) [B4-11, B4-12]

title: Micron says the silicon gap between HBM and DDR5 is widening
supports: HBM3E ~3x DDR5 wafer area per bit, not improving (Micron, Hot Chips 2026) (CROSS-REF from dram-moonshot Phase A logs; not re-opened by B4) [B4-11, B4-12, B4-15, B4-21]

title: Samsung, SK hynix reconsider hybrid bonding timeline
supports: HBM hybrid bonding delayed; 16-high HBM4E earliest (CROSS-REF from dram-moonshot Phase A logs; not re-opened by B4) [B4-11]

title: Understanding the security benefits and overheads of emerging industry solutions to DRAM read disturbance (PRAC)
supports: PRAC <13% overhead now, up to 94% for future chips (CROSS-REF from dram-moonshot Phase A logs; not re-opened by B4) [B4-10]

title: Revisiting RowHammer (ISCA 2020)
supports: HCfirst fell to 4.8K for LPDDR4-1y (CROSS-REF from dram-moonshot Phase A logs; not re-opened by B4) [B4-10]

title: RPU -- A Reasoning Processing Unit
supports: HBM energy model validated vs 3.44 pJ/bit HBM3E; activation ~0.18 pJ/bit streaming (CROSS-REF from dram-moonshot Phase A logs; not re-opened by B4) [B4-12, B4-15, B4-19]

title: Coverage of Bill Dally remarks at GTC 2026
supports: HBM4 ~3-4 pJ/bit; ~2.5 pJ/bit interposer path (CROSS-REF from dram-moonshot Phase A logs; not re-opened by B4) [B4-07, B4-14]

title: Hot Chips 2026: Samsung LPDDR5X-PIM
supports: LPDDR5X-PIM 614 vs 76.8 GB/s (8x), 3.01x throughput Llama-3.1-8B (CROSS-REF from dram-moonshot Phase A logs; not re-opened by B4) [B4-09, B4-19]

title: Samsung embeds AI accelerator in memory chip (HBM-PIM)
supports: HBM-PIM per-bank 300 MHz FP16 units (CROSS-REF from dram-moonshot Phase A logs; not re-opened by B4) [B4-09]

title: Analyzing GPU Energy Consumption in Data Movement and Storage
supports: Data movement up to 84% of A100 dynamic energy, DRAM the largest part (CROSS-REF from dram-moonshot Phase A logs; not re-opened by B4) [B4-18, B4-21]

title: 77 K DRAM retention: weak-row replacement (JSTS 2022)
supports: DDR3 8Gb at 77 K: excluding six weak rows raises refresh time from 8 s to 4096 s -- retention set by a few weak rows and by temperature (CROSS-REF from dram-moonshot Phase A logs; not re-opened by B4) [B4-02, B4-13]

title: CryoGuard: a near refresh-free robust DRAM design for cryogenic computing
supports: When refresh is cut, normal accesses can behave like row hammer (CROSS-REF from dram-moonshot Phase A logs; not re-opened by B4) [B4-02, B4-03]

title: Samsung 10a 4F2 VCT working die
supports: Samsung 4F2 IGZO VCT die with periphery wafer-bonded underneath, 2028 target (CROSS-REF from dram-moonshot Phase A logs; not re-opened by B4) [B4-14]
